Hypocritical

hip-uh-KRIT-ih-kul -- from hypocrite + -ical. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

To be hypocritical is to be guilty of condemning in others the very thing you do yourself.

It seemed deeply hypocritical for the senator to lecture the public about wasteful spending while flying a private jet paid for by donors.

Worked Example

The coach benched players for arriving five minutes late, yet he himself strolled into practice late almost every single day -- a hypocritical double standard his team noticed immediately.

Hypocritical behavior means condemning or criticizing something in others while doing the exact same thing yourself -- the key is the gap between what someone says and what they actually do.

How Hypocritical Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

insincere

insincere: not genuinely feeling or believing what is expressed

two-faced

two-faced: showing one attitude in public and a contradictory one in private

Antonyms

consistent

consistent: acting the same way in similar situations, matching one's words

genuine

genuine: authentic; sincerely meant

How Strong Is It? — inconsistent → hypocritical → two-faced

inconsistent vs. hypocritical

inconsistent vs. hypocritical: Inconsistent simply means not matching up, without necessarily implying dishonesty.

two-faced vs. hypocritical

two-faced vs. hypocritical: Two-faced goes further than hypocritical, suggesting an intentional, deceptive difference between a public and private self.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — hypocrite-

root — hypocrite-: a person who claims standards their own actions contradict (Greek hypokrites, 'stage actor')

suffix — -ical

suffix — -ical: having the qualities of; pertaining to

Put it together

Put it together: Hypocritical comes from hypocrite -- Greek hypokrites, originally 'a stage actor,' someone literally playing a part -- plus -ical. Hypocritical behavior means condemning in others exactly what you do yourself, like an actor playing a role that doesn't match who they really are.

Use the root in a new word: hypocrisy

Word Choice

Hypocritical is a serious moral accusation -- reserve it for real contradictions between what someone preaches and how they actually behave, not just for someone who simply changes their mind.
